ideas.title: What If Your Birthday RSVP Arrived on a Wooden Tablet?
ideas.era: Roman Britain, museum catalog date AD 97/103
ideas.premise: What if today Pip received a fictional office birthday invitation on thin wood, like the surviving invitation from Claudia Severa to Sulpicia Lepidina?
ideas.benchmark_query: What If Your Birthday RSVP Arrived on a Wooden Tablet? history

cast_gags.crow: Opens the book to the actual invitation reference.
cast_gags.pip: Looks for an imaginary accept button on a wooden prop.
cast_gags.mia: Separates the real personal invitation from the invented corporate event.
cast_gags.rex: Calls the fictional office birthday mandatory without attributing that rule to Rome.
cast_gags.timmy: Delivers an absurdly large blank reply while the adults search for the send icon.

rationale.curiosity: A concrete surviving record creates an immediate modern mismatch; this is editorial judgment, not measured audience demand.
rationale.cast_comedy: The fictional cast actions create a problem, attempted fix and physical payoff while preserving their roles.
rationale.modern_contrast: Present-day technology or office rules are explicit comic inventions, never claims about the original artifact.
rationale.primary_sources: Identified original objects or documents are separated from catalog summaries and later institutional interpretation; access still needs checking.

sources.institution: British Museum via Google Arts & Culture
sources.verification_scope: Official source and stated anchors, not automatic semantic entailment

ideas.fact_boundary: The modern office party is fiction; the original is a personal invitation, not proof of compulsory birthday attendance. No earliest-ever handwriting superlative, invented historic dialogue or claim that every line was written by Severa.
research_questions: [VERIFICAR] Read the museum translation and distinguish scribal text from the later hand before quoting words or dating an individual line.
